title: SIGSEGV in on_stream_close() from multi in combination with nghttp2
body: Trying to upgrade to recent curl releases causes very sporadic crashes on embedded systems in the field. I cannot reproduce them consistently, but curl_multi_perform() ends with SIGSEGV in on_stream_close() through nghttp2_session_close_stream. The crash appears near access to the HTTP/2 stream data. curl 7.86.0 avoids the behavior, while the affected build is curl 8.0.1-DEV with nghttp2 1.52.0 on an aarch64 Linux 4.9.337 embedded system. I can apply debug patches or test potential changes.

symptoms_visible: Recent curl builds very sporadically crash in on_stream_close() while my application is inside curl_multi_perform(); the backtrace passes through nghttp2_session_close_stream.
I see the crashes on aarch64 embedded systems in the field and have not found a consistent local reproduction; reverting to curl 7.86.0 avoids them.
N0.label: N0 sporadic HTTP/2 stream-close crash reported

symptoms_visible: With curl 8.2.1 and nghttp2 1.55.1, field devices still very rarely crash in on_stream_close(); reverting curl to 7.86.0 still avoids the crash.
N1_x.label: N1_x current-release update aftermath

symptoms_visible: With curl 8.5.0 and nghttp2 1.58.0, I still get a rare SIGSEGV in on_stream_close(); the backtrace again passes through nghttp2_session_close_stream.
N2_x.label: N2_x related-fix update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The custom libcurl application can now trigger the same rare on_stream_close() crash in an internal test.
On weak connections, a timed-out request is reported complete and its easy handle is closed; later activity on the HTTP/2 session is followed by the crash.
N3.label: N3 stale stream lifecycle evidenced

symptoms_visible: After applying the proposed patch, one affected setup ran for 16 hours without any crash where it would normally see six or seven.
My curl 8.5.0 build with the same patch ran for two days without an on_stream_close() crash, although the test volume was limited.
N4.label: N4 candidate patch verified

symptoms_visible: My pre-merge build with the patch ran for two days without the crash, and a maintainer reports that the change is now present in master; I have not reported a separate retest of the merged release build.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix merged after candidate verification

solution.intent: Assume the HTTP/2 crash was already corrected by the numerous changes since the affected development build and update to a current curl release.
solution.concrete_example: First deploy a current curl and nghttp2 release, since the HTTP/2 implementation has changed substantially, and watch the field devices for recurrence.

edges.comment: Reporter c14-c15: the original reporter installed curl 8.2.1 with nghttp2 1.55.1 and still received an on_stream_close() backtrace; reverting curl to 7.86.0 avoided it. This falsifies the earlier belief in c5/c13 that routine updating had probably already fixed the opening reporter's problem.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as the already-fixed related HTTP/2 cleanup problem and update to the newer release containing that earlier fix.
solution.concrete_example: Try the newer curl release that contains the related HTTP/2 fix and monitor the same field workload.

edges.comment: Reporter c24/c28: after participant3 suggested the crash was related to an issue fixed in curl 8.5.0, the opening reporter installed curl 8.5.0 with nghttp2 1.58.0 and obtained another matching on_stream_close() crash. The related earlier fix therefore did not resolve this case.

question_patterns: Is this the curl command-line tool or a custom application using libcurl?
Can you describe how your program drives the multi interface?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This is a custom application that calls into libcurl and uses the multi interface.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I only run the curl command-line tool and do not manage easy handles or call the multi API myself.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce it anywhere that would let you add HTTP/2 debug logging?
Do you have a test environment where the same crash can be instrumented?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I just noticed that an internal test can trigger this crash, so I can add more logging and try the HTTP/2 debug callback there.

question_patterns: With debug symbols or crash dumps, what are the pointer values at on_stream_close()?
Can you inspect whether the easy handle and stream pointer are still valid when the callback crashes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In our crash dumps, the Curl_easy *data_s address had already been discarded. The address read from data_s for the HTTP/2 stream was invalid, and writing stream->closed triggered the crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The easy handle and stream allocation are both valid in the dump; the fault is inside nghttp2 before libcurl dereferences either pointer.
The stale pointer is visible at the same callback, but the fault occurs on the next write to the stream structure.

question_patterns: Which HTTP/2 error code is passed to on_stream_close() in the crash reports?
Are the callback error codes consistent across the collected dumps?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The error code was NGHTTP2_STREAM_CLOSED in 317 of 318 reports. The one outlier held NGHTTP2_REFUSED_STREAM.

question_patterns: Can you trace the request lifecycle leading up to the crash, especially completion and easy-handle cleanup?
What happens to the request and easy handle before the later stream-close callback?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On a very weak connection, a request times out. curl_multi_info_read returns its completion message, and my client closes that easy handle. The shared HTTP/2 session continues running.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The easy handle remains allocated and attached until after the stream-close callback; no timeout or early cleanup occurs.
The weak connection uses a different DNS server than our normal test environment.

question_patterns: What does the HTTP/2 trace show when the session later processes that stream?
Does nghttp2 call back for the stream after the application has cleaned up its easy handle?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Later, sometimes about 15 minutes afterward, nghttp2 processes the same stream and on_stream_close() is reached with user data that points to the easy handle I already closed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The later close callback references a different live request, not the easy handle that was already closed.

question_patterns: Can you provide a trace showing the data-done and detach control events around the failed request?
In what order do the HTTP/2 filter's data-done and data-detach events occur?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My added logs show the filter receives CF_CTRL_DATA_DONE before CF_CTRL_DATA_DETACH, and the stream is still present at the first event.

edges.comment: Reporter c28-c30 supplied the current crash and custom-application context. Participant5 c18 supplied the crash-dump pointer and error-code observations. Participant6 c22/c31-c37 supplied the weak-connection, timeout, easy-handle cleanup, delayed callback, and control-event trace. These affected deployments are folded into one simulated user side; participant7's unrelated Curl_llist_insert_next crash is deliberately excluded as directed in c42.

question_patterns: Can you apply the proposed HTTP/2 cleanup patch and run the workload that normally produces several crashes?
Please test the candidate patch under the same weak-connection conditions and report the observed crash count.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After 16 hours with the proposed change, I have not seen a single crash. Normally this setup would have produced six or seven by now.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched build still produced six on_stream_close() crashes during the same 16-hour run.
The patched run lasted 14 hours instead of 16 and still had zero crashes, compared with the usual several.

question_patterns: Can the original affected deployment also test the candidate patch for a sustained period?
Please run your internal or field workload with the proposed patched build and report whether the crash returns.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am running curl 8.5.0 with the proposed changes. I have not seen any crashes in two days, although the amount of testing has been somewhat limited.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My patched curl 8.5.0 build still crashed in on_stream_close() during the first day.

edges.comment: Participant3 c39 requested a local candidate-patch test. Participant6 c40/c45 reported zero crashes for 16 hours versus the usual six or seven, and the opening reporter c47 independently reported two crash-free days with curl 8.5.0 plus the patch. This is pre-landing verification and is therefore modeled as measurement rather than the final solution.

solution.intent: Prevent a delayed nghttp2 stream-close callback from dereferencing an easy handle that the application has already closed: clear the stream's user-data association during HTTP/2 data completion before submitting the reset, add defensive callback checks, land the change, and ask the affected user to verify a build containing it.
solution.concrete_example: When a timed-out HTTP/2 transfer reaches data-done, clear nghttp2's stream user data before submitting the reset so a later on_stream_close() cannot recover the freed Curl_easy pointer; retain the defensive user-data checks and have the affected deployment retest a build containing the landed change.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis connects the raw lifecycle evidence: a timeout completes the transfer, the application legitimately closes the easy handle, but nghttp2 still retains that pointer as stream user data and later invokes on_stream_close(). Concluding that curl must clear the association before submitting the reset is engineer-side synthesis, supported by both the traces and the crash-free candidate tests.

edges.comment: Participant6 c37 described the observed timeout and delayed processing sequence; participant3 c39 formulated the stale-user-data theory and proposed clearing stream user data before nghttp2_submit_rst_stream. The candidate was verified in c45/c47 and merged as part of the changes discussed in c36/c46/c49-c50. The tail only establishes that the fix is in master and had been tested before merge; it does not contain an affected user's post-merge release retest, so terminal user_perceives_resolved remains false.

solution.intent: Prevent a delayed nghttp2 stream-close callback from dereferencing an easy handle that has already been closed by clearing stream user data during HTTP/2 data completion before reset submission, adding defensive callback checks, and requesting verification on a build containing the fix.
solution.concrete_example: Clear nghttp2's per-stream user pointer when the transfer is completed or cancelled, before submitting the stream reset, so a delayed close callback cannot dereference a freed Curl_easy object; then test the change under the affected multi-interface workload.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the ultimately correct stale-stream-user-data fix directly from the opening crash. It skips the newer-version failures, detailed lifecycle traces, dump inspection, and candidate verification that grounded the accepted resolution.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread initially pursued the falsified belief that routine updating had already fixed the crash. It allows an immediately correct proposal to match while explicitly recording the evidence it skips.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: after a timed-out HTTP/2 transfer is completed and its easy handle is closed, nghttp2 can later invoke the stream-close callback with stale per-stream user data pointing to that freed Curl_easy object.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected lifecycle and crash evidence: the discarded easy pointer in dumps, completion and easy-handle cleanup on weak connections, and the delayed on_stream_close() callback for the same stream.
The fix must clear nghttp2's stream user data during HTTP/2 data completion before submitting the stream reset, with defensive validation when on_stream_close() observes user data.
Must not claim that merely upgrading to another recent curl release or relying on the earlier related HTTP/2 fix resolves this case; the crash was reproduced with both curl 8.2.1 and curl 8.5.0.

Must require affected-user verification on a build containing the fix before declaring the deployed issue resolved; the thread has strong pre-merge candidate verification but no separate post-merge release retest from the opening reporter.

persona_hint.experience_level: Embedded-systems libcurl integrator with moderate debugging ability: can rebuild curl, cherry-pick patches, collect native backtraces, add debug callbacks, and run long field-style tests, but initially lacks a deterministic reproduction. Additional affected operators with crash-dump and HTTP/2 trace expertise are folded into the same user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, concise, and cautious about conclusions; reports exact versions and backtraces, accepts instrumentation requests, and validates changes through long-running tests rather than claiming success from a short smoke test.
